introduction: This level targets the combined accelerations of rotating and sliding components (Coriolis), the classification of gears, and the high-speed ratios of Epicyclic gear trains.

core_concepts.title: Coriolis Acceleration
core_concepts.description:
This acceleration component exists whenever a point slides along a link that is simultaneously rotating (e.g., in a Quick Return Mechanism). 
Formula: a_c = 2 * v * omega 
(Where v = velocity of sliding, omega = angular velocity of the rotating link).

core_concepts.title: Types of Gears
core_concepts.description:
1. Spur Gear: Teeth are cut parallel to the axis of rotation. (Used for low speeds, parallel shafts).
2. Helical Gear: Teeth are cut at an angle (helix angle) to the axis. (Used for smooth, high-speed power transmission, but induces axial thrust).
3. Bevel Gear: Used to transmit motion between intersecting shafts (usually at 90 degrees).
4. Worm Gear: Used for non-intersecting, non-parallel shafts. Provides extremely high gear ratios and is often irreversible (self-locking).

core_concepts.title: Gear Trains
core_concepts.description:
1. Simple Gear Train: Only one gear on each shaft.
2. Compound Gear Train: At least one shaft carries more than one gear.
3. Epicyclic Gear Train: The axis of one gear revolves around the axis of another gear. Used to achieve the highest speed ratio in the most compact space (e.g., Automobile Differential).

important_entities.name: The Idler Gear
important_entities.significance: In a simple gear train, inserting an intermediate 'idler' gear has absolutely no effect on the final speed ratio. Its sole purpose is to change the direction of rotation of the output (driven) gear.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Advanced Exam Trap: Examiners often ask for the direction of Coriolis acceleration. To find it, take the sliding velocity vector (v) and rotate it by exactly 90 degrees in the direction of the angular velocity (omega).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever an exam asks for high velocity ratios in extremely compact spaces (like wrist watches or car differentials), the answer is always Epicyclic Gear Train.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite GATE and State AE question: 'Which gear train is predominantly used in the differential gear box of an automobile?' Answer: Epicyclic Gear Train.
